core_obligations: For i = 1, show that C_{C/B/A} is fibred over C_{B/A} with strongly cartesian arrows given by Q' = Q tensor_P P', identify the fibre category of u_1 over P -> B with C_{C/P}, and apply the fibred computation together with constancy of the restrictions (proof lines 1515-1537).

For i = 2, show that C_{C/B/A} is fibred over C_{C/A} and that every fibre of u_2 has a final object (A -> B, Q -> C), then apply the same computation lemma with the initial-final lemma (proof lines 1539-1561).

For i = 3, apply the lower shriek computation lemma to u_3 and F' = g_3^{-1}F, identify the sheaf F'_U as a pullback along Sh(C_{Qbar/B/A}) -> Sh(C_{Qbar/B}), and invoke the polynomial algebra lemma to get the vanishing of higher homology and the degree zero value (proof lines 1563-1582).
Conclude Lg_{i,!} g_i^{-1} = id for i = 1, 2, 3 and hence the second family of identities (proof lines 1506-1512 and 1582-1583).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: with the notation of the three-maps equation, Lg_{i,!} composed with g_i^{-1} is the identity for i = 1, 2, 3, and hence Lpi_! composed with g_i^{-1} equals Lpi_{i,!} for each i (source lines 1506-1512). The proof is a case analysis driven by fibred category structures: for i = 1 it exhibits C_{C/B/A} as fibred over C_{B/A} with fibre category C_{C/P}, applies the fibred-category computation of left derived lower shriek and uses that the restrictions are constant; for i = 2 the analogous fibred structure over C_{C/A} is used together with the existence of final objects in the fibres; for i = 3 the computation lemma for the lower shriek is applied to u_3 with the sheaf g_3^{-1}F, whose values are identified as a pullback along a morphism of topoi, so that the polynomial algebra lemma gives the vanishing of the higher homology groups.
